structured_output.world_model:
W2 empirical, after E032. Tip E027: 5.878 s, 0.7547 on seeds 0-2, held-out about 0.7526, so the real margin is about zero.

Measured regularities:
- Time tracks pixels and FLOPs. Freeze (E028) saved about 0.84 s (14%) for about 0.3 pp.
- The epoch dial costs about 5% of time per 0.5 epoch, for about 0.1-0.2 pp.
- Hyperparameter tweaks (LS, wd, lr, warm-up, Lookahead settings, two-stage LS) are flat to negative. Every booster tried so far (E025, E029, E030, E032) failed.
- Any change to step count or RNG use reshuffles the 3-seed mean by about ±0.2 pp.

Extrapolation: adding 0.5 epoch to the freeze recipe (E028 ran on E023 and got 0.7517 at 5.36 s) costs about 0.3 s and gains about 0.1-0.2 pp. That gives about 5.6 s and about 0.753 on seeds 0-2. This is borderline on accuracy and fast in time.

Pure systems changes (I053) are bit-identical in math, so only time changes, by about -0.05 to -0.1 s.

forecasts.reason: E028 saved about 0.5 s on the E023 base, and +0.5 epoch adds about 0.3 s. Accuracy is near the 0.753 bar, so it is a coin flip.
Math is identical if bit-equal, so accuracy is unchanged. Saves about 0.07 s from the trial-0 warm-up.
I expect a modest time gain and a small accuracy loss, below the noise. Whether the whitening bias already stops early (it does after 3 epochs, which is about 34% of steps) is unclear.
An earlier freeze costs more accuracy, since freezing during the 28 px phase hurts.
This is a diagnostic. The expected fresh-seed mean is about 0.753, and the run itself reports the tip's numbers.
BN folding saves memory traffic, but the freeze recipe isn't kept yet. The BN stats mismatch risk adds accuracy variance.
A diagnostic that changes no recipe, so the tip's numbers stand. The profile will likely show a large non-GEMM share.
Muon is likely worth 0.3 pp or more, and dropping it saves about 2-3% of time.

cruxes: Does the freeze (E028) lose about 0.3 pp on the held-out mean, and does adding 0.5 epoch recover it?
Is the tip's true population mean at or above 0.753? If it isn't, every cut needs an accuracy booster first.
Does a bit-identical systems change in prepare (I053) really remove about 0.07 s of trial-0 cost?
